newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Light hopes to trim workforce.
newsitem.headline: China Light hopes to trim workforce.

text.p: China Light & Power Co Ltd said on Thursday it hoped to reduce its workforce in its generation business group to about 1,050 to 1,100 employees from a current 1,300 and would launch a voluntary departure scheme next month.

"In the generation business group we have 1,300 people and after the reorganisation we project the optimal staff level will be around 1,050 to 1,100," Cecilia Chiu, assistant public affairs manager at China Light, told Reuters.
She said the utility company would announce the details of a "selective voluntary departure scheme" in early March.
"The selective voluntary departure scheme is just one the means. Of course there is natural attrition or other means," Chiu added.
China Light has a total workforce of about 6,100.
Most of the employees in the generation business group work in China Light's power stations, Chiu said.
China Light has four power stations in Hong Kong -- Castle Peak, Black Point, Tsing Yi and Penny's Bay. She said the staff reduction plans were not linked to the Black Point station.

The Hong Kong government asked China Light to submit a report on the costs of deferring units five to eight of the eight-unit Black Point station after a consultant's report recommended a halt or delay in the commissioning of the last four units due to slow growth in electricity demand.
"We are trying to achieve economies of scale by centralising certain functions," said Chiu.
